decisions.executionNote: Key is in left workspace; begin elbow-up left approach with open gripper, adapting mirrored pickup to current key location.
Advance left wrist above key while pitching fingers downward; maintain smooth elbow-up continuation.
Continue toward the left-side key, progressively making the grasp axis downward; watch wrist view for centering.
Finish downward alignment and center left gripper over the key shaft; slow final approach before closing.
Use wrist RGB to refine lateral centering over key shaft; keep open and pause to verify before grasp.
Center near the key bow/shaft junction and close the left fingers gradually; retention remains to be checked visually.
Allow full finger closure, then begin a small test lift; judge grasp by whether the key follows in RGB.
Key appears retained between left fingers; lift over five centimeters with gripper commanded fully closed.
Lifted key remains visible in left fingers. Raise and yaw it toward the central handover area while maintaining left-side clearance.
Continue yawing held key for handover; begin raising the empty right arm in its own elbow-up workspace.
Pause the holding arm to check changed key appearance while the open receiving arm continues its safe approach.
RGB shows the key dropped onto the left table. Reopen left fingers and return for a deeper shaft grasp; hold the other arm clear.
Reorient open left fingers across the fallen key shaft and lower toward a secure grasp height.
Continue aligning jaw direction with the fallen key while descending conservatively; retain receiver clear.
Align shaft along the finger approach direction, with small descent; stop to assess centering at grasp height.
Reduce yaw increments after continuity guard; continue open-finger alignment and shallow descent from measured pose.
Center a deeper shaft segment within the left fingertips and begin closing, avoiding further large wrist yaw near its joint limit.
Hold pose and command full closure to secure the regrasp before any lift or rotation.
Test the deeper regrasp with a straight lift, keeping left fingers fully closed and the receiver clear.
Secure key follows lift. Raise toward handover height and unwind wrist away from its limit while retaining full closure.
Keep secure grasp while unwinding left wrist and lifting; bring empty right hand toward central receiving posture with clearance.
Set held key at receiving height with bow toward the right hand; continue receiver orientation while keeping separation.
Hold left key steady and guide open right fingers horizontally toward its exposed bow, stopping short for visual alignment.
Complete receiving orientation and advance partway toward the bow, reducing opening for a controlled handover.
Advance right fingertips toward the exposed bow at matching height; left grip stays closed until receiver is visually seated.
Seat right fingertips farther around the bow and begin closing; keep the left hand fixed and closed for support.
Close receiving fingers fully around the bow while both wrists stay still; verify support before releasing the left grasp.
Gradually release left fingers while the right grip stays fully closed; inspect the key for transfer rather than assuming retention.
Key is visibly slipping rather than retained by receiver. Clear the open right fingers and observe where it settles for recovery.
Recover the settled key with left hand; descend open above it while moving the receiver slightly farther clear.
Aim farther along the shaft so the bow remains exposed for a less crowded transfer; lower open left gripper conservatively.
Align key shaft in wrist view and shift grasp away from bow; begin closure only after settling to shaft height.
Correct lateral offset and close around the exposed shaft, leaving the bow below the fingers for transfer.
Let fingers finish closing on shaft, then make a small vertical retention test without changing orientation.
Lift the shaft grasp and align the exposed bow toward the waiting right hand, keeping left fingers fully closed.
Raise retained key toward receiver height while bringing right fingers closer, leaving a visible gap until vertical alignment is confirmed.
Wrist RGB shows receiver above the exposed bow. Lower right fingers toward its height while advancing only slightly; holder stays fixed.
Use receiver wrist image to reduce remaining height offset and approach exposed bow slowly, without releasing the supporting grasp.
Bow remains offset in receiver view; make another small downward and inward adjustment before closing.
Key has shifted near right fingers; attempt a centered receiving closure immediately while keeping both wrists otherwise steady.
Key has fallen flat. Clear the receiver and reopen the left gripper for a fresh aligned pickup; do not assume transfer succeeded.
Clear the receiving arm farther right and align open left fingers across the flat key shaft for recovery.
Center the shaft between the fingers using wrist view and begin a shallow flat-key grasp, keeping the right arm clear.
Reopen and slightly raise to avoid pushing the flat key; make a small lateral correction to center its shaft before closing.
Lift fingers clear of the tabletop before lateral recentering; the key appears to have been pushed during low adjustments.
Increase tabletop clearance and use a small forward translation to resolve centering direction without disturbing the key.
With clearance restored, align the key shaft vertically in the wrist image before translating into a new grasp.
Translate above the key using wrist-image centering while keeping height and orientation fixed.
Correct the wrist-view translation direction and center the flat key beneath the open left fingers, maintaining clearance.
Approach the centered shaft with modest downward and lateral corrections, checking scale and fingertip alignment before closure.
Shaft is now near the closing region in wrist view. Make a shallow final descent and close without further sweeping motion.
Finish closing at the current shaft location, then perform a small straight test lift to check retention.
The key stayed on the table after test lift. Reopen and move the grasp region toward the visible shaft, then approach again.
Raise clear and unwind the left wrist to align the shaft lengthwise with the fingers, avoiding another diagonal edge grasp.
Continue wrist alignment above the flat key with fingers open and no tableward translation.
Raise substantially to avoid fingertip sweep against the table while continuing yaw alignment for a lengthwise grasp.
At increased clearance, finish aligning the key lengthwise in the wrist view before a straight pickup approach.
Translate at clearance to center the lengthwise key in wrist view; use the corrected image-axis directions before descending.
Separate the receiving arm to prevent wrist contact, and bring left fingers above the current key using the head view for the approach.
Hold the receiver after its continuity guard; continue left-only approach toward the key's current table position with small increments.
Correct the approach toward the key in the wrist image, moving forward at fixed height before closing.
